---
title: "Hydroworld_rivers_ffr to HydroBASINS Mapping"
format: html
---



```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(sf)
library(tidyverse)

world_rivers_ffr <- readRDS("/capstone/netzerohydro/data/cleaned_v1/world_rivers_ffr.rds")

# BasinATLAS Layers
st_layers("/capstone/netzerohydro/data/raw/BasinATLAS_Data_v10.gdb/BasinATLAS_v10.gdb")

# Load BasinATLAS_12
basinatlas_lvl12 <- st_read("/capstone/netzerohydro/data/raw/BasinATLAS_Data_v10.gdb/BasinATLAS_v10.gdb", 
                            layer = "BasinATLAS_v10_lev12")

# Load BasinATLAS_5
basinatlas_lvl5 <- st_read("/capstone/netzerohydro/data/raw/BasinATLAS_Data_v10.gdb/BasinATLAS_v10.gdb", 
                            layer = "BasinATLAS_v10_lev05")

# Load BasinATLAS_4
basinatlas_lvl4 <- st_read("/capstone/netzerohydro/data/raw/BasinATLAS_Data_v10.gdb/BasinATLAS_v10.gdb", 
                           layer = "BasinATLAS_v10_lev04")

# Load BasinATLAS_3
basinatlas_lvl3 <- st_read("/capstone/netzerohydro/data/raw/BasinATLAS_Data_v10.gdb/BasinATLAS_v10.gdb", 
                           layer = "BasinATLAS_v10_lev03")

# Load BasinATLAS_2
basinatlas_lvl2 <- st_read("/capstone/netzerohydro/data/raw/BasinATLAS_Data_v10.gdb/BasinATLAS_v10.gdb", 
                           layer = "BasinATLAS_v10_lev02")
```
# Within logic

```{r}
config_pfaf <- "6" #"622" # Mekong example 4429 # Amazon 6629

# 1. Get all Level 12 IDs inside your target Level 4 basin
target_l12_ids <- basinatlas_lvl12 |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  dplyr::filter(
    stringr::str_starts(
      format(PFAF_ID, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE, justify = "none"),
      config_pfaf
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::transmute(hybas_l12 = sprintf("%012.0f", as.numeric(HYBAS_ID))) |>
  dplyr::pull(hybas_l12)

# 2. FILTER RIVERS (In-Basin): First, find which river systems touch the basin
rivers_in_basin <- world_rivers_ffr |>
  dplyr::mutate(hybas_l12_chr = sprintf("%012.0f", as.numeric(hybas_l12))) |>
  dplyr::filter(hybas_l12_chr %in% target_l12_ids)

# --- NEW STEP: GET FULL SYSTEMS ---
# Identify unique main_riv IDs from the basin and pull their full global geometry
target_main_rivs <- unique(rivers_in_basin$main_riv)

plot_rivers_full <- world_rivers_ffr |>
  dplyr::filter(main_riv %in% target_main_rivs)
# ----------------------------------

# 3. FILTER BASIN: Boundary for the background map
plot_basin <- basinatlas_lvl3 |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_starts(format(PFAF_ID, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE, justify = "none"), config_pfaf))

# 4. MAP IT
ggplot() +
  # Basin Background: Thicker border (1.2) to act as a "frame" for the full network
  geom_sf(data = plot_basin, fill = "#bbcde5", color = "#222222", linewidth = 1.2, alpha = 0.4) +
  
  # Full River Systems: Reaches are no longer clipped to the basin
  geom_sf(data = plot_rivers_full, aes(color = as.factor(main_riv)), linewidth = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "turbo") + 
  labs(
    title = paste("Pfaf digits used:", config_pfaf),
    subtitle = paste("Unique main_riv found:", length(target_main_rivs))
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

```{r}
library(osmdata)

# 1. Get the bounding box of your basin
basin_bbox <- st_bbox(plot_basin)

# 2. Fetch OSM water polygons (Lakes, Reservoirs, Wide Rivers)
osm_water <- opq(bbox = basin_bbox) |>
  add_osm_feature(key = "natural", value = "water") |>
  osmdata_sf()

# 3. Plot the "Quick OSM" Layer Cake
ggplot() +
  # Base: OSM Water polygons (Low contrast background)
  geom_sf(data = osm_water$osm_polygons, fill = "#bbcde5", color = NA, alpha = 0.5) +
  # Mid: Your chosen basin boundary
  geom_sf(data = plot_basin, fill = NA, color = "#222222", linewidth = 0.6) +
  # Top: Your specific main_riv reaches (High contrast highlight)
  geom_sf(data = plot_rivers, color = "#1c5d99", linewidth = 0.8) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = paste("HydroRIVERS Network vs. OSM Water Context:", config_pfaf))
```


```{r main_riv-to_basin}
#  1. Find all reaches in main_riv 
river_groups <- world_rivers_ffr %>%
  group_by(main_riv)

#  2. Find most downstream reach (pour point) 
river_outlets <- river_groups %>%
  slice_min(dist_dn_km, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

#  3. Match basin to pfaf_id 
river_to_basin_lookup <- river_outlets %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(main_riv, hybas_l12) %>%
  left_join(
    basinatlas_lvl12 %>% 
      st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      select(HYBAS_ID, PFAF_ID), 
    by = c("hybas_l12" = "HYBAS_ID")
  )
#  4. Identify main_riv within any given basin level 
get_rivers_in_basin <- function(target_pfaf_id, lookup_table) {
  lookup_table %>%
    dplyr::filter(stringr::str_starts(PFAF_ID_STR, as.character(target_pfaf_id))) %>%
    dplyr::pull(main_riv)
}

config_pfaf <- "6221" 

# 1. Update the river list and filter
selected_rivers_ids <- get_rivers_in_basin(config_pfaf, river_to_basin_lookup)

# Filter spatial data: grabs every reach (hyriv_id) sharing a main_riv
plot_rivers <- world_rivers_ffr %>% 
  dplyr::filter(main_riv %in% selected_rivers_ids)

# Filter basin: also uses the scientific notation fix for the polygon
plot_basin <- basinatlas_lvl4 %>%   
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_starts(format(PFAF_ID, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE), config_pfaf))

# 2. Map it
ggplot() +
  # Basin fill and outline (Carbon Black)
  geom_sf(data = plot_basin, fill = "#bbcde5", color = "#222222", linewidth = 0.6) +
  # River networks (Baltic Blue)
  geom_sf(data = plot_rivers, color = "#1c5d99", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = paste("Basin Hierarchy View:", config_pfaf),
       subtitle = paste("Main River Systems found:", length(selected_rivers_ids))) +
  theme_void()
```

```{r}
river_system_directory <- world_rivers_ffr |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(main_riv == 60443230) |>
  # Join with basin metadata to get the Pfafstetter addresses
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(basinatlas_lvl12), by = c("hybas_l12" = "HYBAS_ID")) |>
  select(main_riv, hybas_l12, PFAF_ID) |>
  distinct() |>
  mutate(PFAF_TEXT = format(PFAF_ID, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE))

# View the result
knitr::kable(head(river_system_directory))
```
